official_questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
I. W.P. Scott defined divorce as 'an institutionalised arrangement for terminating the marriage relationship and allowing each partner the right to remarry'.
II. The first legislation in respect of the dissolution of marriage in India was enacted in 1869, and is 'Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act'.
III. The irresponsible departure from the home on the part of husband, leaving the family to fend for itself is called as 'the poor man's divorce'.
Which of the above given statements are correct ?
official_questions.core_fact: W.P. Scott defined divorce as institutionalised termination with right to remarry; India's first divorce law was the Indian Divorce Act 1869 (Christians); desertion is called 'the poor man's divorce'.

statements.t: W.P. Scott defined divorce as 'an institutionalised arrangement for terminating the marriage relationship and allowing each partner the right to remarry'.
The first legislation on dissolution of marriage in India was enacted in 1869 and is the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act.
statements.fact: The 1869 law is the Indian Divorce Act (for Christians); the Parsi Act dates from 1865 (re-enacted 1936).

statements.t: Irresponsible departure of the husband leaving the family to fend for itself is called 'the poor man's divorce'.

official_questions.rule: Divorce laws: Parsi 1865/1936; Indian Divorce Act 1869 (Christians); Dissolution of Muslim Marriages 1939; HMA 1955; SMA 1954.
official_questions.key_note: Note: the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act 1865 predates 1869; the key's logic rests on the 1869 Act being the Indian Divorce Act.

official_questions.stem: Ravindra and Seema are husband and wife. Krishna and Madhavi are children of Ravindra-Seema. Madhavi is married to Harish and Jyothi is the daughter of Madhavi-Harish. Then the Consanguineous Kinship is between :
official_questions.core_fact: Consanguineous kin are related by blood (descent); affinal kin by marriage. Krishna (Madhavi's brother) and Jyothi (Madhavi's daughter) are maternal uncle and niece – blood kin.

statements.t: Consanguineous kinship exists between Ravindra and Seema.
Consanguineous kinship exists between Madhavi and Harish.
Consanguineous kinship exists between Krishna and Jyothi.
Consanguineous kinship exists between Krishna and Harish.

official_questions.rule: Kinship: consanguineal = blood (parent, sibling, uncle-niece); affinal = through marriage (spouse, in-laws).

statements.t: The sapinda prohibition upheld by the Delhi High Court is in Section 4(a) of the Hindu Marriage Act.
The sapinda prohibition upheld by the Delhi High Court is in Section 5(v) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

statements.fact: S.12(1)(a) covers voidable marriages for impotence.

statements.t: The sapinda prohibition upheld by the Delhi High Court is in Section 13(ii) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

official_questions.rule: HMA S.5: (iv) prohibited degrees, (v) sapinda; S.11 void; S.12 voidable; S.13 divorce.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following was the custom practised during the ancient period that allows married women to cohabit with a designated male for the sole purpose of procreating a child if her husband was impotent or had died ?
official_questions.core_fact: Niyoga allowed a widow or wife of an impotent husband to beget a child by an appointed man (often the husband's brother) solely for progeny.

statements.t: The ancient custom allowing a wife to cohabit with a designated male to procreate is Apastamba.

The ancient custom allowing a wife to cohabit with a designated male to procreate is Pratigya.
The ancient custom allowing a wife to cohabit with a designated male to procreate is Niyoga.

official_questions.rule: Niyoga (procreation); Anuloma/Pratiloma (hypergamy/hypogamy); eight forms of Hindu marriage.
